commit.message:
rpc : typed request helpers and a single validation step on the server (#32651)

* rpc : typed request helpers and a single validation step on the server

Client and server share one table (rpc_msg_types) that maps each
fixed-size command to its request and response structs. The client sends
them with dispatcher->call<CMD>() and call_async<CMD>(), the server serves
them with rpc_serve<CMD>(), so the per-command code in rpc_serve_client
and at the call sites is gone and a wrong struct for a command does not
compile. SET_TENSOR, SET_TENSOR_2D and GRAPH_COMPUTE get header structs,
written with rpc_writer and parsed with a bounds-checked rpc_reader. The
wire format is unchanged.

Validation of client data is now in one place:
- deserialize_tensor rejects what ggml_new_tensor would assert on (op
  range, ne[0] not a multiple of the block size, element count overflow)
  and computes the tensor size without overflow before the buffer check
- rpc_check_region replaces the per-handler bounds checks and checks the
  request against the tensor size, which ggml_backend_tensor_set/get/memset
  assert on, so an in-buffer but out-of-tensor request no longer aborts
- graph_compute builds the graph in one pass over the tensors, which the
  client sends in topological order: no recursion, and unknown or
  duplicate ids, duplicate nodes, sources sent after their users, compute
  nodes with unallocated operands and views outside their view_src buffer
  are rejected; a tensor may be its own source (ggml_cast)
- GET_ALLOC_SIZE fails if a source tensor is invalid
- a client-sized allocation that fails closes the connection instead of
  terminating the server

* rpc : trim comments
